items.label: SpaceX
items.headline: Starship’s first integrated test in April 2023 was so powerful it tore apart the concrete beneath its launch pad and hurled debris hundreds of metres — by Flight 13 in July 2026, its upper stage was travelling more than 16,000 kilometres from Texas before touching down so gently in the Indian Ocean that it remained intact and afloat.
items.summary:
Across 13 integrated tests, Starship moved from breaking its own launch pad to guiding an intact upper stage into a distant ocean landing zone.

items.headline: On 18 August, SpaceX logged its 100th launch of 2026, hitting that mark two months faster than it did in 2024 — a company that flew 25 times in 2020 is now lifting off more than three times a week
items.summary:
The routinization of spaceflight is reshaping what's possible in orbit—and challenging our intuitions about technological breakthroughs.
